The Fixer's diagnosis is correct. Plain Text (TextStringSimpleNode) answers GetTextLayoutResult through ParagraphLayoutCache.slowCreateTextLayoutResultOrNull (foundation 1.10.0-alpha04, l.366-402). That method lays out a new MultiParagraph at prevConstraints.copyMaxDimensions() (the full max width) but reports size = layoutSize (the shrink-wrapped node size). So didOverflowWidth (size.width < multiParagraph.width) is true for every text narrower than its constraint, such as 'UploadNavKey' at 1x. The replacement check still detects truncation. I proved this with mutations in a scratch worktree, running only ShellChromeScreenshotTest. (A) TmrCapsText with softWrap=false, maxLines=1 and width(30.dp): both tests fail with '1 Profile overflows its width: line right 429.0 > 90'. This is the real onTextLayout layout, where the paragraph is unbounded and its size is constrained. (B) The top-bar action Text with softWrap=false, maxLines=1 and width(24.dp): both fail with 'Save overflows its height', because the semantics re-layout exceeds maxLines. (B2) The same without maxLines: both fail with 'Save overflows its height', because the re-layout wraps to more lines than the node height. At head, both tests pass. No baseline was re-recorded in this commit. Remaining blind spot: clipping by an ancestor, which neither this check nor the original hasVisualOverflow could see.
